nodes.name: SBD-DC01
nodes.known: Primary domain controller with AD and DNS. In this design it holds the PDC emulator role, so it is the domain's authoritative time source: it serves time from its own clock, and every other member follows the domain hierarchy (F09).
design: Protect identity administration from lower-trust workstation sessions.
Restrict directory and DNS changes; monitor privileged changes.
Test directory recovery and replication health.
Serve domain time as the reliable source from its own clock; turn off hypervisor time synchronization for the domain controller VMs.
Define how the clock is checked against an approved reference and corrected, its drift threshold, and its fallback, without an external network connection.
evidence: Account and privilege reviews; AD/DNS configuration.
Replication checks, audited changes, and recovery exercise records.
Time design, scheduled drift checks and corrections, and time hierarchy test results.

nodes.name: SBD-DC02
nodes.known: Listed as the secondary domain controller with AD and DNS. This label does not establish a passive standby role or identify the PDC emulator.
design: Verify the intended replication and DNS redundancy design.
Apply the same privileged-access protections as SBD-DC01.
Keep tested backups; replication alone is not a backup.
evidence: Replication and DNS failover tests.
Domain controller backup and restoration evidence.

nodes.name: SBD-SUBCA01
nodes.known: Subordinate / issuing CA. CA type, domain membership, certificate templates, and publication endpoints are not specified.
design: Constrain enrollment rights and permitted certificate purposes.
Protect CA private keys and separate CA administration.
Define certificate revocation, CRL/AIA publication, and recovery procedures.
evidence: Certificate policy, enrollment permissions, and issuance logs.
Key protection and certificate-revocation tests.

nodes.name: SBD-DHCP01
nodes.known: Windows Server with two roles: DHCP for the VLAN 80 pool, and Network Policy Server for 802.1X port admission (EAP-TLS with machine certificates). NPS handles port admission only; router logins stay named local accounts.
design: Define approved scopes, reservations, DNS options, and lease policy.
Restrict administrative changes and monitor lease events.
Plan relay behavior explicitly if clients occupy separate VLANs.
Require machine certificates from the issuing CA; no password-based EAP. Unknown devices go to quarantine VLAN 90.
evidence: Approved DHCP settings and administrative access review.
Lease logs and client addressing tests.
Network policy export and admission tests: enrolled PC admitted, unknown device quarantined.

nodes.name: SBD-FS01
nodes.known: File share server. Shares, data sensitivity, access groups, and encryption settings are not provided.
design: Grant share and filesystem permissions through approved roles.
Protect sensitive data in transit and at rest according to policy.
Back up data and test restoration of both data and permissions.
evidence: Share and filesystem access reviews and denial tests.
Encryption configuration and restoration evidence.

nodes.name: SBD-APPS01
nodes.known: License server and application tier. It runs the vendor licensing service for approved clients (F12) and the application API that SBD-WEB01 calls over HTTPS (F21), and it is the only registered SQL consumer (F22).
design: Expose only the vendor-required licensing services to approved clients.
Restrict service identity and administrative privileges.
Document vendor ports, configuration, and recovery requirements.
Accept application API calls from SBD-WEB01 only, and connect to SBD-SQL01 under a managed service identity with least-privilege database roles.
evidence: Vendor-supported flow matrix and configuration.
Service account permissions and approved client list.
Application API and encrypted SQL connection tests from the registered callers.

nodes.name: SBD-SQL01
nodes.known: SQL server for the application tier. SBD-APPS01 is its only registered consumer (TCP 1433 with TLS, F22); SBD-WEB01 is explicitly denied (F14), and no workstation path exists.
design: Allow only identified consumers and approved management paths.
Use narrowly scoped database roles and protect sensitive data.
Test database, key, and configuration recovery together.
evidence: Database permission reviews and approved consumer matrix.
Transport, storage, key-management, and restore test evidence.

nodes.name: SBD-SYSLOG01
nodes.known: Log-message collection server. Sources, collection agents, transport, and routing to Splunk or the audit repository remain to be confirmed.
design: Collect the defined event types from supported sources.
Use protected transport where supported and required.
Monitor delivery failures, time alignment, and collector capacity.
evidence: Source-to-collector tests and event coverage.
Transport settings and log-delivery failure alerts.

nodes.name: SBD-AUDIT01
nodes.known: Audit log repository. Retention, tamper protection, backup, and ingestion routes are not yet specified.
design: Separate log administration from administration of audited systems.
Define retention and protect against unauthorized alteration or deletion.
Test search, export, and recovery of retained records.
evidence: Repository permissions and retention configuration.
Integrity checks and retrieval tests.

nodes.name: SBD-SPLUNK01
nodes.known: Splunk SIEM server. A server name alone does not establish log coverage, detection rules, or a response process.
design: Validate relevant source coverage and detection logic.
Assign review and investigation responsibilities.
Test alerts and escalation; manage false positives and gaps.
evidence: Detection tests, log coverage, and review records.
Investigation tickets and escalation procedures.

nodes.name: SBD-EPO01
nodes.known: Trellix ePO and DLP management server. Agent deployment, protection modules, licensing, and policy enforcement are not verified.
design: Restrict who can change or disable endpoint and DLP policies.
Verify the relevant agents and protection modules are installed and enforcing policy.
Test policy updates, health reporting, and authorized data-flow restrictions.
evidence: Agent coverage and policy enforcement tests.
Management access reviews and alert/investigation records.

nodes.name: 50 Windows PCs
nodes.known: Fifty Windows user workstations, displayed as one selectable group. Individual hostnames and domain-join status were not provided.
design: Apply approved hardening and minimize local administrative access.
Deploy and verify patching, protection, and required logging.
Use separate protected workflows for privileged administration.
evidence: Configuration and patch compliance reports.
Endpoint protection coverage and local administrator reviews.

nodes.name: AdminJumpBox01
nodes.known: Dedicated Tier 0 administrative host for AD, DNS, PKI, and every system that can control them: the core switch, the hypervisor hosts, and the DC-facing scopes of WSUS, ePO, Nessus, and Splunk. No member-server or endpoint administration.
design: Use separate Tier 0 admin accounts and offline-compatible MFA.
Restrict targets to Tier 0 systems and scopes; root CA ceremonies remain local.
evidence: Privileged target allowlist and account reviews.
MFA, audit, and cross-tier denial tests.

nodes.name: SBD-WSUS01
nodes.known: Windows Server Update Services server. Upstream source, approval rings, client groups, and signing configuration remain unspecified.
design: Approve and test updates before deployment.
Verify update provenance, integrity, and delivery settings.
Track missing updates, failures, exceptions, and remediation deadlines.
evidence: Update approvals and testing records.
Client patch reports and exception reviews.

nodes.name: SBD-REPO01
nodes.known: Linux repository server. Package consumers, repository content, upstream sources, and signing practices are not provided.
design: Restrict repository publication and synchronize only approved sources.
Validate package signatures and document trust and key changes.
Monitor repository changes and protect credentials.
evidence: Repository configuration and signature verification tests.
Publisher permissions and change history.

nodes.name: SBD-NESSUS01
nodes.known: Vulnerability management server. Scan scopes, schedules, credentials, and agents are not specified.
design: Authorize target scope and constrain scanner access and credentials.
Analyze findings and track remediation and exceptions.
Rescan to validate fixes; exclude the offline root from network scans.
evidence: Authorized scan plan and credential protection settings.
Findings, remediation records, and validation scans.

nodes.name: SBD-ROOTCA01
nodes.known: Offline, non-domain-joined root certificate authority. It has no live network edges in this diagram.
design: Keep routine operation disconnected from all network segments.
Use a controlled offline ceremony for subordinate signing and root CRL publication.
Protect private keys, backup media, and physical access; test recovery.
evidence: Key ceremony and certificate policy records.
Physical/media controls and protected recovery tests.

nodes.name: SBD-PKI-MGMT01
nodes.known: Certificate templates are directory objects. This host provides the administrative tools to manage them.
design: Separate enrollment approval from template administration.
Review template permissions and certificate purposes.
evidence: Template export and permission review.
Enrollment approval and denial tests.

nodes.name: SBD-WEB01
nodes.role: Internal Apache web server · Linux, domain-joined
nodes.known: Linux with Apache, joined to the domain with SSSD like Splunk and Nessus. Serves the internal web application over HTTPS and calls the application API on SBD-APPS01; it has no database dependency.
design: Permit only approved internal consumers; call the application API on SBD-APPS01, never the database.
Harden the web service and maintain trusted certificates; patch from SBD-REPO01 and send syslog over TLS.
evidence: Service configuration and approved flow matrix.
TLS, access-control, and web-to-SQL denial tests.

nodes.name: SBD-MGMT01
nodes.known: Management tools. Define administrative accounts, permitted targets, and protocols.
design: Maintain an approved configuration baseline and inventory.
Track changes and constrain management scope.
evidence: Configuration baseline and asset register.
Approved change records and access reviews.

nodes.name: SBD-ADMIN-SRV01
nodes.known: Privileged workstation for approved member-server targets. Separate operator roles further restrict security tools and protected audit storage. It hosts one virtual machine, SBD-ADMIN-PC01, the Tier 2 seat: Tier 1 accounts work only on the host, Tier 2 accounts only in the virtual machine.
design: Separate privileged accounts from identity and endpoint administration.
Require offline-compatible MFA, named targets, and session auditing.
Host the Tier 2 seat as a virtual machine under the DISA Windows PAW STIG exception for sites short on workstations, sharing no clipboard, drives, or folders with it.
evidence: Target allowlist and effective host rules.
Cross-tier denial and MFA tests.
Virtual machine placement, host and guest settings, and refused sign-ins in both directions across that boundary.

nodes.name: SBD-ADMIN-PC01
nodes.known: Privileged workstation for the 50 client endpoints, running as a virtual machine on the SBD-ADMIN-SRV01 seat with its own name and address. No AD, CA, or server administrative sessions, and no higher-tier sign-ins.
design: Use scoped endpoint-admin identities and managed local credentials.
Deny direct management from ordinary user workstations.
Deny Tier 0 and Tier 1 sign-ins inside the virtual machine; keep Tier 2 accounts off the host.
evidence: Endpoint scope and privileged account review.
Server and identity management denial tests.
Refused higher-tier sign-in inside the virtual machine.

vlans.name: Domain controllers
vlans.boundary: Restrict directory administration; allow only documented identity and DNS dependencies.

vlans.name: Identity & services
vlans.boundary: Define DHCP relay and approved update and collection routes. No internet upstream.

vlans.name: PKI infrastructure
vlans.boundary: Only the issuing services join this segment. The offline root has no switch connection.

vlans.name: Servers & data
functions: Database services for the application tier
Licensing, application API, and internal web services
vlans.boundary: Authorize each client-to-service path. The fleet reaches SBD-WEB01 (F13), SBD-WEB01 calls the application API on SBD-APPS01 (F21), and only SBD-APPS01 reaches SBD-SQL01 (F22); web-to-SQL is denied (F14). Licensing uses each application’s registered vendor port (F12). All four servers share this VLAN, so host firewalls enforce these rows.

vlans.name: Security & monitoring
vlans.boundary: Scope scanners and agents explicitly. Protect audit records and separate security administration.

vlans.name: Tiered administration
vlans.boundary: Separate identity/PKI, server, and endpoint administrative hosts and accounts: two physical seats, with the endpoint seat a virtual machine on the server seat. Host rules deny cross-tier management; sharing this VLAN does not grant access.

vlans.name: Management tools
vlans.boundary: Constrain publishers and management identities. Validate packages brought in on approved media.

vlans.name: User workstations
functions: Internal identity, files, and approved updates
802.1X port admission; unknown devices go to quarantine VLAN 90
vlans.boundary: Dedicated client segment. Block peer SMB/RDP and direct administrative access; allow documented identity and resource dependencies only.

facilities.name: Core switch stack
facilities.detail: Internal Layer 3 switching and inter-VLAN routing. Access control lists enforce documented exceptions; segmentation alone does not establish enforcement.
items: Default deny between VLANs; explicit source, destination, service, purpose, and owner for exceptions.
Host firewalls also enforce isolation within VLANs 40, 50, 60, and 80.
The VLAN 80 DHCP relay (F04) forwards client broadcasts to SBD-DHCP01; verify relay and scope settings after changes.
Test allowed sessions and blocked lateral movement; back up approved rules.
Management plane: switch management only on VLAN 100 from AdminJumpBox01, named administrator accounts, switch syslog (including denies) to SBD-SYSLOG01, and versioned configuration backups.

facilities.name: Controlled media handling
facilities.detail: Inbound: approve source and media, scan and validate content, record custody, then let an authorized operator import it. Outbound: approve release, review content and destination, record the export, then physically carry the approved media.
items: No cable, data diode, or automatic transfer crosses the air gap.
Use write protection where appropriate to the approved procedure.
Keep inbound and outbound handling distinct; sanitize media under MP-6.

facilities.name: Offline backup & recovery
facilities.detail: Keep protected offline copies of required information, system configurations, and recovery material. Define retention, custody, recovery priorities, and restoration responsibilities.
items: Test restoration of AD/DNS, PKI, files, SQL, and network configuration.
Splunk, Tenable/Nessus, and Trellix ePO/DLP each remain one server: no cluster or standby.
Protect each platform’s configuration, required data, keys, and recovery material; validate vendor-supported recovery.
Define downtime, recovery point and recovery time targets; rehearse loss of each platform.
Backup path: each server writes to a protected local backup volume; custodians carry DC, CA, and audit backups here under the media custody procedure. There is no network path to this facility.

Document the single-instance design in the system security plan, with backups as its mitigation (PL-2): one server each suits the small network and modest resource needs. The risk response records the remaining risk (RA-7), and only the authorizing official accepts it (CA-6); track restore gaps in the POA&M (CA-5).

scenarios.label: Sign in
scenarios.title: A workstation finds its identity.
scenarios.caption: Addressing, name resolution, and domain authentication.
scenarios.assumption: Domain-joined Windows workstation using internal addressing, DNS, and authentication services.

steps.title: Obtain a network address
steps.description: A new client requests an address and receives lease settings. The exchange includes discovery, offer, request, and acknowledgement.
steps.note: Rule F04: the core relays VLAN 80 broadcasts to SBD-DHCP01, which leases from the 10.0.80.100–199 pool.

steps.title: Locate directory services
steps.description: The workstation asks internal DNS to locate domain services. DNS records connect service names to reachable hosts.
steps.note: DC01 handles this request. DC02 also provides DNS; configure the client resolver order.

steps.title: Authenticate to the domain
steps.description: The client proves its identity to the domain controller’s Key Distribution Center and obtains a ticket-granting ticket.
steps.note: Domain membership, account state, DNS, and time configuration must support authentication. This does not grant access to every resource.
steps.wire: Kerberos encrypts tickets and key material

steps.title: Read directory information
steps.description: The workstation reads its computer and policy objects from Active Directory, then fetches Group Policy from SYSVOL over SMB. Rule F03 permits the full directory profile for domain members.
steps.note: LDAP signing and channel binding are required. A Kerberos (SASL) bind lets Windows sign and seal the session; LDAPS uses TLS instead.
steps.wire: Signed and sealed with the Kerberos session key

scenarios.label: Open a file
scenarios.title: From a name to an authorized file.
scenarios.caption: Follow a domain client to its file share.
scenarios.assumption: Kerberos-based SMB access by a domain client. Cached DNS and tickets can remove steps from the exchange.

steps.title: Resolve the file server
steps.description: The client resolves the file server’s name before opening a connection. The diagram uses SBD-FS01 as the named destination.
steps.note: Configure the service DNS records and authorized share paths.

steps.title: Request a service ticket
steps.description: The workstation uses its ticket-granting ticket to request a ticket for the file service. It then presents that service ticket to the server.
steps.note: Service identity and name resolution must agree. Authentication and file authorization are separate decisions.
steps.wire: Kerberos encrypts tickets and key material

steps.title: Open the approved share
steps.description: The client requests a file over SMB. The server applies the relevant share and filesystem permissions before allowing access.
steps.note: Replies return on the same session. Share names, data classification, and encryption settings remain undefined.
steps.wire: SMB signing or encryption per data policy

scenarios.label: Get updates
scenarios.title: Bring updates inside. Distribute with care.
scenarios.caption: A disconnected update workflow, with no internet edge.
scenarios.assumption: Internal WSUS distribution through approved deployment rings and controlled media imports.

steps.title: Import approved update material
steps.description: An authorized operator brings approved update material across the air gap using controlled media and an established import process.
steps.note: An authorized operator performs the transfer using approved removable media.

steps.title: Check update metadata
steps.description: The client contacts the internal WSUS service for update metadata using the TLS-enabled configuration.
steps.note: Verify server certificate trust and configured client policy. Reference ports can be changed.

steps.title: Retrieve signed update content
steps.description: WSUS uses its HTTP connection for update payloads, with signatures protecting payload authenticity. TLS is used for metadata rather than every WSUS path.
steps.note: Requests travel to WSUS; content travels back. Validate content signatures and approved deployment settings.

scenarios.label: Follow a log
scenarios.title: Turn an event into useful evidence.
scenarios.caption: From Windows and Linux sources to collection, analysis, and retention.
scenarios.assumption: Windows events arrive by event forwarding and Linux events by syslog over TLS. The collector forwards to Splunk for analysis and archives a protected copy on SBD-AUDIT01.

steps.title: Forward a domain controller event
steps.description: SBD-DC01 pushes the subscribed security events to the collector. The collector never reaches into the source: the subscription is source-initiated, set by Group Policy.
steps.note: Kerberos authenticates both ends and encrypts the message body, even on port 5985. Rule F17 permits every domain member to forward.

steps.title: Deliver a source event
steps.description: A configured Linux source can initiate a protected syslog session to the collector. The connection uses TLS transport.
steps.note: Verify sender / receiver support, peer identity, certificate trust, and queue behavior.

steps.title: Ingest for investigation
steps.description: The forwarder on the collector sends the Windows events and syslog intake to Splunk for indexing, searches, and alerts.
steps.note: Rule F10. The forwarder queues events while Splunk is down and replays them afterwards; alert on a stopped source.

steps.title: Retain an audit copy
steps.description: On schedule, the collector writes dated archive files to the repository share on SBD-AUDIT01. Each archive is hashed and cataloged on arrival.
steps.note: Rule F11. The archival account can write but not delete; only the audit custodian’s separate accounts manage retention.

scenarios.label: License check
scenarios.title: A licensing service has its own contract.
scenarios.caption: Follow the client request to its licensing service.
scenarios.assumption: APPS01 provides licensing on each application’s registered vendor port (F12), recorded in the register per application.

steps.title: Request a license
steps.description: An approved client contacts the licensing service to check or obtain its entitlement. Protocol, direction, persistence, and offline behavior depend on the product.
steps.note: Rule F12 permits each application’s registered vendor port. The application API that SBD-WEB01 calls and APPS01’s database connection are separate rows (F21, F22).

scenarios.label: Offline trust
scenarios.title: The root stays outside the live network.
scenarios.caption: A controlled offline certificate ceremony.
scenarios.assumption: No live root CA connection exists. Signing artifacts move only through an approved, human-controlled offline process.

steps.title: Prepare the signing material
steps.description: Prepare the subordinate CA’s signing request and the records required for the ceremony. Protect the request and validate the intended certificate policy.
steps.note: The root and issuing CA are separate trust responsibilities. Domain membership and CA type are not established.

steps.title: Use the offline root
steps.description: Authorized operators use the protected root key in a controlled ceremony. The root CA remains non-domain-joined and disconnected.
steps.note: Keep the root physically disconnected and restrict use of its private key to authorized ceremonies.

steps.title: Return publication artifacts
steps.description: Return approved certificate and revocation artifacts through the documented offline transfer process. Define the issuing CA’s enrollment and publication design separately.
steps.note: Transfer root signing artifacts manually. Define internal CRL/AIA publication endpoints and enrollment transports.

scenarios.label: Use a web app
scenarios.title: A browser trusts the internal web service.
scenarios.caption: Name resolution, certificate trust, revocation, and an encrypted session.
scenarios.assumption: A domain workstation opens an approved internal web application on SBD-WEB01 under rule F13. Clients already trust the internal root certificate and check revocation at pki.sbd.test (F18).

steps.title: Resolve the web server
steps.description: The browser resolves the web service’s internal name before connecting. DNS returns SBD-WEB01’s address on VLAN 40.
steps.note: DC02 also provides DNS. Publish the service name in internal DNS and keep it consistent with the name on the server certificate.

steps.title: Verify the server certificate
steps.description: The browser opens a TLS session. SBD-WEB01 presents a certificate from the internal issuing CA, and the client checks the name, validity dates, and chain to the trusted offline root.
steps.note: Trust comes from the root certificate already distributed to clients, not from a network path to the root. Next, the client checks whether the certificate has been revoked.

steps.title: Check revocation
steps.description: The client follows the CRL distribution point in the certificate to pki.sbd.test on SBD-PKI-MGMT01 and downloads the issuing CA’s current revocation list.
steps.note: Rule F18. The CRL is signed by the issuing CA, so plain HTTP is the standard transport: tampering is detected, and nothing secret is sent.

steps.title: Request the application
steps.description: Inside the encrypted session, the browser sends HTTP requests and receives the application’s responses. The application decides what the signed-in user may see.
steps.note: TLS protects the connection; the application still authenticates and authorizes each user. Behind the page, SBD-WEB01 calls the application API on SBD-APPS01 (F21), and only SBD-APPS01 queries SBD-SQL01 (F22).

whatIfs.label: DC01 is down
whatIfs.title: One domain controller fails.
whatIfs.caption: The client turns to SBD-DC02 for DNS and authentication.
whatIfs.assumption: SBD-DC01 is offline. Clients list both domain controllers as DNS servers, and SBD-DC02 provides DNS and Kerberos for the domain.

steps.title: Query SBD-DC01
steps.description: The workstation sends its DNS query to its first configured DNS server. SBD-DC01 is offline, so no reply comes back.
steps.note: The request is permitted (F01), but a server that is down cannot answer. The client waits for its timeout.

steps.title: Retry with SBD-DC02
steps.description: The client retries with its next configured DNS server. SBD-DC02 also provides DNS for the domain and answers.
steps.note: This works only if clients list both domain controllers as DNS servers and the DNS zone replicates to both.

steps.title: Authenticate with SBD-DC02
steps.description: DNS service records list both domain controllers, and the client’s domain controller locator finds SBD-DC02 responding. SBD-DC02’s Key Distribution Center issues the ticket-granting ticket.
steps.note: The locator ping (LDAP over UDP 389) and the rest of the directory profile, including Group Policy and SYSVOL, use rule F03 against SBD-DC02 as well. After the outage, restore SBD-DC01 and confirm replication.
steps.wire: Kerberos encrypts tickets and key material

whatIfs.label: Certificate expired
whatIfs.title: The browser refuses an expired certificate.
whatIfs.caption: Trust checks fail before any application data is sent.
whatIfs.assumption: SBD-WEB01’s server certificate has passed its validity end date. The network path is unchanged and still permitted by rule F13.

steps.title: Resolve the web server
steps.description: The browser resolves the web service’s internal name, exactly as on a normal day.
steps.note: Name resolution is unaffected by certificate problems.

steps.title: Present an expired certificate
steps.description: SBD-WEB01 presents a certificate whose validity period has ended. The browser checks the dates, stops the connection, and shows a certificate error.
steps.note: The network permitted the session (F13); the failure is in certificate validation on the client. Renew server certificates through the issuing CA before they expire.

policy.label: F13 · Permitted, then refused by the client

whatIfs.label: A PC tries SQL
whatIfs.title: Default deny stops a direct database connection.
whatIfs.caption: No exception exists for workstation-to-SQL traffic.
whatIfs.assumption: A user workstation attempts a direct connection to SBD-SQL01. The policy register has no workstation-to-SQL exception.

steps.title: Connect straight to SBD-SQL01
steps.description: A workstation tries to reach the database server directly. The core finds no matching exception, so default deny drops the session.
steps.note: Clients reach data through approved applications, not direct database connections. This denial is one of the boundary acceptance tests.

whatIfs.label: PC-to-PC remote desktop
whatIfs.title: Host firewalls stop lateral movement.
whatIfs.caption: One workstation tries remote desktop to another.
whatIfs.assumption: Two user workstations share VLAN 80. Traffic between them is switched within the VLAN and never crosses the core’s routed boundary, so each workstation’s host firewall enforces the policy.

steps.title: Open remote desktop to another PC
steps.description: A workstation tries a remote desktop session to a peer on the same VLAN. The destination’s host firewall refuses it.
steps.note: Rule D02 denies peer RDP and D01 denies peer SMB. Attackers use these paths to move from one compromised PC to the next.

whatIfs.label: Attack drill
whatIfs.title: An intruder tests every boundary.
whatIfs.caption: Six moves an intruder might try, from one compromised PC to a stolen admin session. Each is checked against the rules.
whatIfs.assumption: One user workstation is compromised. Each step replays an acceptance test from the security design against the same policy register as the rest of the model.

steps.title: A compromised PC tries the database
steps.description: Malware on one workstation reaches straight for SBD-SQL01. No exception exists for workstation-to-SQL traffic, so the core drops the attempt.
steps.note: Clients reach data through approved applications, never directly.
steps.test: Client-to-SQL, client-to-management, and peer SMB/RDP fail.

steps.title: It looks for the security tools
steps.description: Taking over a security tool would blind the defenders. The PC tries Splunk’s web interface. No rule lets user workstations reach security-tool management, so default deny drops it.
steps.note: Port 8000 is the Splunk Web default; confirm the configured port. The same rule applies to the Nessus and ePO consoles.
steps.test: A compromised client cannot reach security-tool management interfaces.

steps.title: It tries a neighbor’s file shares
steps.description: Next, the PC tries the shares on another workstation in VLAN 80. The traffic never crosses the core, so the neighbor’s host firewall refuses it.
steps.note: Rule D01 denies peer SMB. Attackers use administrative shares to copy tools from one PC to the next.
steps.test: Client-to-SQL, client-to-management, and peer SMB/RDP fail.

steps.title: It tries remote desktop to a neighbor
steps.description: The PC tries a remote desktop session to a peer. The destination’s host firewall refuses it.
steps.note: Rule D02 denies peer RDP. Host firewalls matter here because traffic inside a VLAN never reaches the core.
steps.test: Client-to-SQL, client-to-management, and peer SMB/RDP fail.

steps.title: A compromised web server reaches for the database
steps.description: If SBD-WEB01 were taken over, SBD-SQL01 would be the next target. They share VLAN 40, so the core never sees this traffic. SBD-SQL01’s host firewall refuses it.
steps.note: Rule F14 denies web-to-SQL: SBD-WEB01 has no database dependency, because it reaches data through the application API on SBD-APPS01 — the only registered SQL consumer (F21, F22).
steps.test: The web server cannot reach SQL directly; only SBD-APPS01, the registered consumer, connects.

steps.title: A stolen admin session aims at a domain controller
steps.description: With an endpoint administrator’s stolen session on SBD-ADMIN-PC01, the attacker aims at SBD-DC01. That seat, a virtual machine on SBD-ADMIN-SRV01, manages user endpoints only. No rule lets it manage a domain controller, so default deny drops it.
steps.note: Tiered administration keeps one stolen account from reaching every tier: the management rule for ADMIN-PC01 (A03) names only the user endpoints.
steps.test: An endpoint administrator cannot manage a DC, issuing CA, or member server.

policy.transport: TCP/UDP 53
policy.purpose: Internal name resolution for every networked system

policy.transport: TCP/UDP 88 · password change TCP/UDP 464
policy.purpose: Domain authentication for every domain member

policy.transport: LDAP TCP/UDP 389 · LDAPS 636 · GC 3268/3269 · SMB 445 (SYSVOL, Group Policy) · RPC 135 + 49152–65535 (NetLogon)
policy.purpose: Directory, Group Policy, and domain operations; LDAP signing and channel binding required. Linux members (SSSD) use DNS, Kerberos, and LDAP

policy.transport: UDP 67/68 · the core relays VLAN 80 broadcasts to SBD-DHCP01
policy.purpose: Address leases for the VLAN 80 pool, 10.0.80.100–199, through the core DHCP relay

policy.transport: TCP 445; signing/encryption per data policy
policy.purpose: Approved share access; filesystem authorization still applies

policy.transport: TLS 8531 metadata; 8530 signed payloads
policy.purpose: Approved Windows updates by ring: pilot, workstations, member servers, then domain controllers

policy.transport: TCP 6514; mutual trust and sender allowlist
policy.purpose: Linux event collection from SBD-REPO01, SBD-SPLUNK01, SBD-NESSUS01, and SBD-WEB01

policy.transport: UDP 123 · domain hierarchy
policy.purpose: Domain members sync from the domain controllers, and SBD-DC02 from the PDC emulator; Linux members use chrony or ntpd to the DCs

dc1.purpose: Find services, authenticate identities, and answer directory requests.

services.name: Kerberos KDC
services.note: Password changes use TCP / UDP 464.

services.name: Directory access
services.note: UDP 389 carries the domain controller locator ping. Client and protection settings determine the binding.

services.name: RPC services
services.note: NetLogon, LSA, and SAM use the dynamic range after the endpoint mapper.

services.name: Domain time
services.note: Members follow the domain time hierarchy.

services.name: AD Web Services
services.note: Used by Active Directory PowerShell and Administrative Center from the Tier 0 administration host (rule A01), not user workstations.

dc1.dependencyText: Check DNS, time, replication, and recovery design together. SBD-DC01 holds the PDC emulator role in this design: it is the domain's authoritative time source, serving time from its own clock, and every other domain member syncs from the domain controllers (F09).
verify: DNS and directory discovery from a client.
Replication health and protected restore procedures.

dc2.purpose: Provide another AD DS and DNS service point.

services.name: Kerberos KDC
services.note: Password changes use TCP / UDP 464.

services.name: Directory access
services.note: UDP 389 carries the domain controller locator ping. Client and protection settings determine the binding.

services.name: RPC services
services.note: NetLogon, LSA, and SAM use the dynamic range after the endpoint mapper.

services.name: Domain time
services.note: Members follow the domain time hierarchy.

services.name: AD Web Services
services.note: Used by Active Directory PowerShell and Administrative Center from the Tier 0 administration host (rule A01), not user workstations.

dc2.dependencyText: Another domain controller is not merely a passive standby. Confirm site placement, replication, DNS behavior, and role ownership.
verify: Client behavior when one DC is unavailable.
Replication and directory recovery tests.

dhcp.purpose: Provide client lease settings for the approved address space, and admit devices to VLAN 80 ports with 802.1X.

services.name: DHCPv4
services.note: The core relays VLAN 80 broadcasts here (F04); the pool is 10.0.80.100–199.

services.name: RADIUS (NPS role)
services.note: Only the VLAN 80 access switch is a RADIUS client.

services.name: 802.1X EAP-TLS
services.note: No password-based EAP methods.

dhcp.dependencyText: Scopes, address options, leases, relay placement, and failover need an explicit design. The NPS role checks machine certificates from the issuing CA and computer accounts in AD; unknown devices go to quarantine VLAN 90, which has no routes.
verify: Lease acquisition and renewal.
Configured DNS options and relay behavior.

fs.purpose: Serve shared files while enforcing resource permissions.

services.name: SMB
services.note: Reference service port; share and encryption policies are unspecified.

fs.dependencyText: Use domain-based identity and name resolution. Define share names, access groups, and data sensitivity.
verify: Allowed and denied access by role.
File, permission, and encryption-key restoration.

apps.purpose: Answer licensing requests from approved clients and application API calls from SBD-WEB01; the only registered SQL consumer.

services.name: License manager
services.note: Recorded per application in the register.

services.name: Application API
services.note: Called by SBD-WEB01 only.

services.name: Database client
services.note: The only registered SQL consumer.

apps.dependencyText: SBD-WEB01 calls the application API, and SBD-APPS01 alone connects to SBD-SQL01. All three share VLAN 40, so host firewalls enforce these rows.
verify: Licensing from approved clients on the registered port.
API calls from SBD-WEB01 only, and the encrypted SQL connection.

sql.purpose: Host the application databases for SBD-APPS01, the only registered SQL consumer.

services.name: SQL Database Engine
services.note: Default instance. Only SBD-APPS01 connects (F22); SBD-WEB01 is denied (F14).

sql.dependencyText: SBD-APPS01 is the only consumer (F22). No workstation, web-server, ePO, or WSUS database dependency exists on this server; within VLAN 40, SBD-SQL01’s host firewall enforces F22 and the F14 deny.
verify: TLS-encrypted connections from SBD-APPS01; refusals from SBD-WEB01 and the workstations.
Database permissions, transport protection, and restore tests.

syslog.purpose: Receive and route the chosen log messages.

services.name: Syslog over TLS
services.note: Configure the collector listener and trusted senders.

services.name: Splunk forwarder
services.note: Queues events while Splunk is down and replays them afterwards.

services.name: Audit archive
services.note: Write-only archival account to SBD-AUDIT01.

syslog.dependencyText: Define downstream delivery, buffering, acknowledgements, and loss handling.
verify: End-to-end event arrival and timestamp quality.
Collector outage and backlog recovery.

splunk.purpose: Linux, domain-joined. Single server instance, sized for a small network; no cluster or standby. Index and investigate the security events that are actually collected.

services.name: Splunk ingestion
services.note: Forwarded Windows events and router syslog from SBD-SYSLOG01.

splunk.dependencyText: SBD-SYSLOG01 forwards to it under rule F10. Configure indexing, storage, parsing, time handling, and detection coverage.
verify: Searchable source events and parsing.
Detection tests and investigation workflow.

audit.purpose: Windows, domain-joined. Retain security records under the approved retention policy.

services.name: Audit archive
services.note: Write-only archival account from the collector (F11); hashes cataloged on arrival.

audit.dependencyText: The collector writes dated archives to the repository share. Only the audit custodian’s separate accounts manage retention; offline copies follow the recovery practice.
verify: Record retrieval across the retention period.
Unauthorized-change prevention and recovery.

wsus.purpose: Distribute approved Windows updates inside the air gap.

services.name: Signed update payloads
services.note: WSUS uses separate metadata and payload connections.

wsus.dependencyText: Clients are the illustrated consumers. Content arrives through a human-controlled boundary transfer; no live upstream path is drawn.
verify: Client policy, certificate trust, and approvals.
Payload signatures and installation results.

repo.purpose: Serve the approved Linux package collection.

services.name: Package repository
services.note: GPG-signed packages and metadata for the domain-joined Linux servers.

services.name: Log forwarding
services.note: Syslog over TLS to the collector (F07).

repo.dependencyText: SBD-SPLUNK01, SBD-NESSUS01, and SBD-WEB01 install packages only from here (F19). Import and publication need approved media handling and signing-key controls.
verify: Package signature validation and allowed publishers.
Repository content and log delivery.

subca.purpose: Issue certificates under the approved subordinate CA policy.
subca.dependencyText: Root trust is a certificate relationship and controlled offline process, not a network dependency. Templates, CA type, and domain membership are unknown.
verify: Enrollment permissions and certificate purpose.
Revocation publication and CA recovery.

root.purpose: Protect the trust anchor and perform authorized offline ceremonies.

services.name: Live network listeners
services.note: Offline and non-domain-joined.

root.dependencyText: Signing and publication artifacts are handled through a controlled manual process. No network scan or remote administration path exists in this model.
verify: Private-key custody and physical access.
Ceremony records and tested recovery.

epo.purpose: Single Trellix ePO/DLP server instance, sized for a small network; no cluster or standby. Manage the chosen endpoint protection and DLP policies.

services.name: Agent check-ins
services.note: Agents on every Windows system start the connection; with peer-to-peer and RelayServer off, endpoints open no listener for the server.

epo.dependencyText: Agents on every Windows system check in for policy and report events (F16). Agent policy for the domain controllers is a Tier 0 scope, changed only from AdminJumpBox01.
verify: Agent inventory and policy application.
Tamper controls and protection alerts.

nessus.purpose: Linux, domain-joined. Single Tenable/Nessus server instance, sized for a small network; no cluster or standby. Assess authorized targets for known vulnerabilities.

services.name: Credentialed scanning
services.port: SMB 445 and WMI to Windows · SSH 22 to Linux
services.note: Rule F15: scheduled scans of the approved target list; the DC scan credential is Tier 0.

nessus.dependencyText: Rule F15 covers the approved targets inside the scan window; plugins arrive on approved media. The offline root is excluded from network scans.
verify: Authorized scan scope and credential protection.
Finding validation and remediation rescan.

web.purpose: Serve approved internal web applications over HTTPS.

services.name: HTTPS
services.note: Server certificate issued by the internal issuing CA.

services.name: Application API client
services.note: Its only back-end dependency; it has no database connection.

web.dependencyText: Linux with Apache, joined to the domain with SSSD. Clients find the service through internal DNS and trust its certificate through the internal PKI. Data comes through the application API on SBD-APPS01 (F21); a direct connection to SBD-SQL01 is denied (F14). Packages come from SBD-REPO01 (F19), and logs leave as syslog over TLS (F07).
verify: HTTPS from approved clients with a trusted, unexpired certificate.
Blocked access from unapproved sources, and a refused direct connection to SQL01.

jump.purpose: Provide dedicated Tier 0 administration: identity, PKI, and every system that can control them.

services.name: Remote management
services.port: RDP 3389 · WinRM 5985–5986 · AD Web Services 9389 to the DCs · SSH 22 to Linux · HTTPS consoles
services.note: Rule A01: Tier 0 targets only, with MFA and named accounts.

jump.dependencyText: Targets are DC01, DC02, the issuing CA, PKI template administration, the core switch, the hypervisor hosts, and the DC-facing scopes of WSUS, ePO, Nessus, and Splunk. ADMIN-SRV01 handles member servers, and ADMIN-PC01, a virtual machine on it, handles clients; this seat runs no virtual machines. Host firewalls and scoped accounts deny cross-tier access.
verify: Approved target list and privileged identities.
Session controls and administrative audit trail.

workstations.dependencyText: VLAN 80 uses the 10.0.80.100–199 client pool. Configure hostnames and domain membership. Each PC’s host firewall blocks peer SMB/RDP (D01, D02) and accepts management only from SBD-ADMIN-PC01 and the scanner.
verify: Effective configuration and allowed applications.
Patch results, local privileges, and logging coverage.
